title: Add a packed CPU bitset baseline before escalating CUDA complexity
hypothesis: Before CUDA/Tensor-Core complexity is considered useful for Boolean Fourfold composition, a packed CPU representation should be measured under the same exact revision-bound subject. Python bigint row bitsets may remove enough interpreter overhead that the CUDA crossover moves materially upward or disappears for sparse/small workloads.

design.authority: TypedRelationBlock plus BooleanSemiring remains the executable semantic oracle
design.physical_baseline: one Python integer bitset per CSR row
design.composition: for each set middle bit in the left row, OR the corresponding packed right-row support
design.output: reconstruct one canonical Boolean TypedRelationBlock with the same subject, typed axes and relation semantics
design.reuse: ProbeCase, deterministic Fourfold fixture, reference operation count, CUDA memory estimator and atomic report writer are reused from cuda_boolean_probe.py

measurements: exact stdlib CSR oracle cost when inside the reference operation bound
CUDA dense-memory estimate for the same case as a complexity/context comparison

bounds.case_contract: reuses ProbeCase bounds from the CUDA experiment

verification.integrated_contract_surface: success in all four matrix jobs
verification.bitset_calibration_step: success on Python 3.12 / PYTHONHASHSEED 0 for all six bounded cases
verification.repository_collection: success; collection-only, not a complete repository execution claim
verification.full_suite: manual-only and not executed by this pull-request run
verification.gpu_execution: not part of this packet and not claimed

acceptance: packed row masks preserve exact CSR support
packed Boolean composition matches the stdlib CSR oracle exactly on the focused verified case
canonical output digest matches the oracle when the same relation name is used
the report remains authority=diagnostic-only and claim=none
the existing workflow executes the bounded CPU baseline without adding another workflow family

interpretation.reason: The CI step proves the calibration executes and remains semantically exact; timing values are environment-specific diagnostics and were not promoted into a comparative claim in this packet.
interpretation.decision_use: A future GPU/Rust experiment must compare against this simpler packed-CPU arm, not only against the high-overhead stdlib CSR reference path.

kill_or_redesign: packed support ever differs from the stdlib Boolean oracle
packing/canonicalization dominates so strongly that repeated-query residency has no plausible break-even
a simpler existing preindexed Forest/relation-dictionary path remains equally expressive and cheaper for the target workload
a Rust bitset implementation cannot improve materially over the Python-bigint calibration while adding maintenance cost
